newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday October 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday October 25.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Leaders of the three main trade unions, CGIL, CISL and UIL were not satisfied with answers to their questions at talks with the government. A new meeting is expected on Monday. CGIL leader Sergio Coffertati says in an interview "We had only partial and inadequate answers from the labour pact to the Eurotax". If talks fail on Monday "we will decide the shape and form of a mobilisation" (La Stampa).

* Prime Minister Romano Prodi says in an interview that there is no crisis with trade unions. He is considering a TV message to the country to explain the 1997 budget and the advantages of getting into the EMU (La Repubblica).
* In the parliamentary budget commission, majority parties and opposition find an agreement over tax modifications in the 1997 budget but tension remains high over the "Eurotax" (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi says in an interview that the government does not intend to wait until the full approval by the parliament of the 1997 budget to seek the re-entry of the lira into the ERM. "The timing could be after the vote in the lower house" in mid-November (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* State industrial holding IRI supports the view of telecom holding STET that Telecom Italia's new cordless phone does not abuse its dominant position in fixed-line telephony, as suggested by the head of anti-trust authority Giuliano Amato (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* The lira and BTP bonds have little reaction to the discount rate cut by the Bank of Italy (all).
* The Treasury decided to increase the total number of shares of energy giant ENI to be offered for sale in the second tranche placement to 1.1 billion shares from 700 million (all).

* Stock exchange watchdog Consob asked for an inquiry over Olivetti share price movements. Consob is said to suspect insider trading sales before the sharp fall of the share price at the beginning of September (Il Sole 24 Ore, Corriere della Sera).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
